item.aggregated_output: {"id":"Q026_protein_kinase_like_function_transfer","track":"held_out","category":"functional_inference","prompt":"Canonical protein kinases, aminoglycoside phosphotransferases, and phosphoinositide 3-kinases have related catalytic-domain architecture in SCOPe. What common evolutionary or mechanistic conclusions are justified, and what evidence is needed before transferring substrate specificity or regulation?"}

item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q026_protein_kinase_like_function_transfer","answer":"SCOPe places these catalytic domains in the alpha+beta class and protein-kinase-like fold d.144; placement in the protein-kinase-like superfamily d.144.1 supports probable remote common ancestry, whereas fold membership alone would establish only architectural similarity. Canonical protein kinases, aminoglycoside phosphotransferases, and phosphoinositide 3-kinases can therefore be inferred to share a related kinase-like catalytic core and broad ATP-dependent phosphoryl-transfer chemistry, including spatially corresponding nucleotide-binding and catalytic elements. Their distinct family-level assignments matter: canonical protein kinases phosphorylate protein residues, aminoglycoside phosphotransferases phosphorylate small-molecule antibiotics, and phosphoinositide 3-kinases phosphorylate membrane phosphoinositides. The shared superfamily does not justify transferring exact substrate specificity, inhibitor sensitivity, catalytic efficiency, cellular role, or regulatory mechanisms among them. Such transfer requires evidence beyond the fold: reliable sequence/profile alignment and phylogenetic placement within the relevant family; active-site and substrate-binding-pocket conservation assessed by structural superposition; appropriate ligand- or substrate-bound structures; biochemical substrate panels and kinetic assays; catalytic and specificity-residue mutagenesis; and, for regulation, evidence from regulatory domains, domain architecture, membranes/localization, interaction partners, and activation experiments. A structurally convenient representative from another family is therefore suitable only as a remote core template, not as a functional or regulatory surrogate.","evidence_used":["pretrained model knowledge"]}]}
